stem:
Omkar draws transversal $t$ across lines $p$ and $q$. At the crossing with $p$, $\angle 1$ sits above $p$ and to the right of $t$. At the crossing with $q$, $\angle 2$ sits above $q$ and to the right of $t$.

Which claim about $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ is correct?

options.text: Call $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ corresponding even if both were chosen from the same crossing with $p$, skipping that one angle must come from each crossing.
Also treat $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ as same-side interior angles and use that interior rule here, beyond matching positions for corresponding angles.
$\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ are corresponding angles: each is above its line and to the right of $t$, so they sit in matching positions at the two crossings.
Call them corresponding only because the printed labels $1$ and $2$ are the standout numbers, without using matching positions.

teacher.key_rationale: Corresponding angles occupy matching positions in the two angle sets made by a transversal. Taking both from one crossing, swapping in same-side interior rules, or grabbing the printed labels all miss that hinge.
